chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Jamil from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who performs zihar with his wife fifteen times, he said: For him are fifteen expiations.

key_terms.ظَاهَرَ: Zihar (verbal divorce where husband compares wife to mother)

ai.seo_question: How many expiations are required if a man performs zihar multiple times?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies the cumulative nature of kaffarah (expiation) in cases of repeated zihar, establishing that each utterance incurs a separate obligation rather than a single lump sum. This ruling is pivotal in Shia fiqh for determining financial liability in marital disputes, reflecting the principle that zihar is treated as a distinct sin per instance. The narration underscores the seriousness of the verbal act, linking it directly to the Quranic mandate of freeing a slave or fasting as atonement.
